title: Ascension narrative from the Mount of Olives
summary: Acts begins with Jesus’ departure from the disciples and their return from the Mount of Olives to Jerusalem. The exact point on the ridge is not identified.

dating.label: after the resurrection narratives; absolute year debated

historicalNote: The atlas maps the named landscape without claiming archaeology can adjudicate the supernatural event or identify an exact footprint.

title: Matthias chosen among the Twelve
summary: Acts places the selection of Matthias within the Jerusalem community before Pentecost.
historicalNote: The upper-room building is not archaeologically identified.

title: Pentecost in Jerusalem
summary: Acts 2 narrates the Spirit coming upon the gathered disciples during Pentecost and a multilingual crowd in Jerusalem.

dating.label: Pentecost after Jesus’ death; commonly placed c. 30–33 CE
dating.note: Absolute chronology depends on the debated year of Jesus’ death.

historicalNote: Jerusalem is secure; Acts does not give a recoverable street address for the initial gathering.

title: Healing at the Beautiful Gate
summary: Acts 3 places Peter and John at a gate called Beautiful and then Solomon’s Portico.
historicalNote: The Herodian Temple complex is secure; the exact gate identity is disputed.

title: Stephen’s speech and stoning
summary: Acts 6–7 culminates with Stephen taken outside the city and stoned.
historicalNote: Paul/Saul is portrayed as approving the execution. No exact execution site is recoverable.

title: Philip in Samaria
summary: Acts 8 narrates Philip preaching in a city of Samaria before later travel south.
historicalNote: Acts says “a city of Samaria” in many translations/manuscript interpretations; the atlas does not force the episode into the city of Sebaste as certain.

title: Philip and the Ethiopian official on the Gaza road
summary: Acts places the encounter on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza, described as desert/deserted. The exact road segment is unknown.
historicalNote: No exact road segment is pinned. Ancient Jerusalem–Gaza travel could use more than one corridor.

title: Saul’s Damascus-road encounter and entry into Damascus
summary: Acts narrates Saul approaching Damascus, experiencing a revelatory encounter, and entering the city blind.

dating.label: commonly placed c. 33–36 CE
dating.note: Pauline chronology is reconstructed; no exact year is stated.

historicalNote: Damascus is certain; the exact road approach and encounter location are not. Paul’s own Galatians 1 describes the calling and later Arabia/Damascus sequence without reproducing Acts’ narrative details.

title: Paul’s visit to “Arabia” in Galatians
summary: Paul says in Galatians that after his calling he went to Arabia and returned to Damascus.
historicalNote: Acts does not narrate this Arabian interval. Its location, duration, and relationship to Nabataean territory remain debated.

title: Paul’s escape from Damascus
summary: Acts and 2 Corinthians preserve related escape traditions from Damascus.
historicalNote: 2 Corinthians mentions an ethnarch under Aretas; the political interpretation and exact chronology are debated.

title: Peter and Cornelius at Caesarea
summary: Acts 10–11 links Peter at Joppa with Cornelius at Caesarea in a pivotal Gentile-inclusion narrative.
historicalNote: Both cities are secure; Cornelius’s house is not archaeologically identified.

title: Antioch community and the name “Christians”
summary: Acts 11 presents Antioch as a major mixed community and says disciples were first called Christians there.
historicalNote: Antioch is secure; Acts is the literary source for the naming notice.

title: Claudian famine and Judean relief context
summary: Acts 11 associates Agabus with a famine prediction and relief sent from Antioch; Josephus independently describes severe famine in Judea during Claudius’s reign.
historicalNote: The independent famine context is real, but matching every literary notice to one exact year is uncertain.

title: Agrippa I persecutes Jerusalem leaders
summary: Acts 12 says Agrippa I executes James son of Zebedee and imprisons Peter.
historicalNote: Agrippa I’s rule is independently attested; the prison-escape narrative is known from Acts.

title: Death of Agrippa I at Caesarea
summary: Acts 12 and Josephus Antiquities 19 both place Agrippa I’s final illness/death at Caesarea, though narrative details and emphases differ.
historicalNote: The shared Caesarea setting and 44 CE death are strong historical anchors; the sources are not identical accounts.

title: First missionary journey from Antioch
summary: Acts 13–14 narrates Barnabas and Paul traveling from Antioch through Cyprus and south-central Anatolia and returning.
historicalNote: The city sequence is textual. Exact roads and dates are reconstructed; Derbe’s modern site identification remains disputed.

title: Sergius Paulus at Paphos
summary: Acts names Sergius Paulus as proconsul of Cyprus during the Paphos episode.
historicalNote: The proconsular office fits Roman Cyprus; inscriptions bearing related names do not by themselves conclusively identify the Acts individual.

title: Paul stoned at Lystra
summary: Acts 14 narrates Paul being stoned and left outside Lystra before continuing to Derbe.
historicalNote: Lystra’s site identification is probable; the exact stoning spot is not recoverable.

title: Jerusalem Council / apostolic meeting
summary: Acts 15 narrates a Jerusalem meeting over Gentile inclusion and Torah obligations.
historicalNote: The relationship between Acts 15 and Paul’s Jerusalem visit in Galatians 2 is debated; the atlas cross-references them without declaring them identical.

title: Second missionary journey
summary: Acts 15:36–18:22 narrates Paul and Silas through Syria/Cilicia and Anatolia, the crossing to Macedonia, Achaia, and return via Ephesus/Caesarea.
historicalNote: The sequence is textual; dates and the inland Anatolian road choices remain reconstructed.

title: Lydia and the Philippian riverside gathering
summary: Acts 16 narrates Lydia’s encounter with Paul’s group by a river outside Philippi.
historicalNote: Philippi is secure; the exact riverside gathering spot is not.

title: Paul and Silas imprisoned at Philippi
summary: Acts narrates imprisonment, an earthquake, and release after the magistrates learn Paul and Silas are Roman citizens.
historicalNote: The prison building is not archaeologically identified.

title: Thessalonica and Berea
summary: Acts 17 narrates synagogue activity and opposition in Thessalonica followed by a move to Berea.

title: Paul in Athens and the Areopagus address
summary: Acts 17 narrates Paul in the agora and before/at the Areopagus, engaging philosophical audiences.
historicalNote: The physical hill is known; “Areopagus” can also denote the council, so the exact speech location remains interpretive.

title: Aquila and Priscilla leave Rome under Claudius
summary: Acts 18 says Aquila had recently come from Italy because Claudius ordered Jews to leave Rome. Suetonius preserves a related expulsion/disturbance notice.
historicalNote: The exact date is usually placed around 49 CE, but Suetonius does not date the episode precisely and “Chrestus” is historically debated.

title: Paul before Gallio at Corinth
summary: Acts 18 places a legal accusation against Paul before Gallio, proconsul of Achaia.
historicalNote: Gallio’s proconsulship is externally anchored by the Delphi inscription, but the inscription itself does not mention Paul and the exact hearing spot within Corinth is not proven.

title: Third missionary journey and return to Jerusalem
summary: Acts 18:23–21:17 narrates travel through Galatia/Phrygia, an extended stay at Ephesus, Macedonia/Greece, Troas, the Aegean coast, and return to Jerusalem.
historicalNote: The textual itinerary is strong at named stops; exact inland roads and sailing tracks are reconstructed.

title: Extended ministry at Ephesus
summary: Acts 19 describes Paul teaching in Ephesus for an extended period, including a hall associated with Tyrannus.
historicalNote: Ephesus is secure; the lecture hall is unlocated and exact chronology is reconstructed.

title: Ephesus theater disturbance
summary: Acts 19 narrates a crowd gathering in the theater amid conflict involving artisans and the Artemis cult.
historicalNote: The theater and Artemision are archaeological facts; the narrative episode is known from Acts.

title: Eutychus at Troas
summary: Acts 20 narrates a nighttime gathering at Troas and Eutychus falling from an upper story.
historicalNote: Troas is secure; the building is not identified.

title: Farewell to Ephesian elders at Miletus
summary: Acts 20 places Paul at Miletus summoning elders from Ephesus and giving a farewell speech.

title: Paul’s Jerusalem arrival and arrest
summary: Acts 21 narrates Paul’s arrival, Temple controversy, arrest by Roman forces, and subsequent hearings.
historicalNote: Jerusalem/Temple/Antonia context is strong; the exact movement through the precinct and custody spaces is not recoverable.

title: Night transfer from Jerusalem to Caesarea
summary: Acts 23 gives a military transfer via Antipatris to Caesarea after a plot against Paul.
historicalNote: The city sequence is explicit; the exact road and overnight facility are not.

title: Paul before Felix at Caesarea
summary: Acts 24 narrates a hearing before Felix and a prolonged period of custody.
historicalNote: Felix and Caesarea’s administrative role are independently historical; the exact hearing room and prison location are not.

title: Paul before Festus, Agrippa II, and Berenice
summary: Acts 25–26 places Paul’s appeal and hearing before Festus with Agrippa II and Berenice at Caesarea.
historicalNote: Festus’s accession is historically real but its exact calendar year is debated, often placed c. 59–60 CE.

title: Voyage from Caesarea toward Rome
summary: Acts 27–28 narrates Paul under guard traveling by sea from Caesarea through the eastern Mediterranean, shipwrecking on Melite/Malta, and continuing to Italy.
historicalNote: The named sequence is textual. The drawn sea track is illustrative because ancient wind, current, and tacking behavior prevent recovery of a single exact line.

title: Decision to leave Fair Havens
summary: Acts 27 narrates debate over wintering at Fair Havens and an attempted move toward Phoenix before the storm.
historicalNote: Fair Havens/Lasea are probable identifications; Phoenix is deliberately left unpinned because harbor identification is disputed.

title: Shipwreck and winter on Malta
summary: Acts narrates shipwreck on Melite, survival ashore, hospitality, and a three-month stay.
historicalNote: Malta is the mainstream island identification; the exact bay, wreck, anchors, and Publius estate are not established archaeological identifications.

title: Paul under house arrest in Rome
summary: Acts ends with Paul in Rome under guard, receiving visitors and teaching for two years.
historicalNote: Rome is secure; the rented lodging is not. Acts does not narrate Paul’s death.

title: Pauline correspondence across the eastern Mediterranean
summary: The Pauline letters address communities and coworkers in Rome, Corinth, Galatia, Ephesus/Asia, Philippi, Thessalonica, and the Lycus Valley. Recipient geography is often more secure than composition-place chronology.
historicalNote: This event-like network record visualizes recipient geography; it does not assert that every traditionally Pauline letter has the same authorship status or one exact composition site/date.
